# PCB mast: build guide

<!-- Generated by docs/make_build_docs.py from builds/pcb/build_doc.csv and the CSVs beside it, common/parameters.csv, builds/pcb/parameters.csv, fab/board_rules.csv and common/layout.py. Do not edit by hand: change the CSVs and rerun the script. -->

Decide, order, check and assemble one PCB mast. The boards, their design and how to regenerate them are in [`README.md`](README.md); the antenna choice is in [`docs/ANTENNA_SELECTION.md`](../../docs/ANTENNA_SELECTION.md). Status: **generated and DRC-clean, not yet ordered or built.**

Labels such as `[Pipe]` or `[PoE splitter]` name the options chosen under Decisions; a row or step with a label belongs to that option only. `[All builds]` rows apply whatever you choose.

> **Unplug PoE before plugging in USB.** All modules share one 5 V rail with no diodes, so a USB cable on a XIAO or the ESP32 while PoE feeds the deck ties the computer's VBUS to the PoE supply. Power from PoE OR from USB, never both. Damage from ignoring this is not covered by anything in this repo; you build and power it at your own risk. More in [README: Deck](README.md#deck).

> **Firmware:** this deck is wired for relay protocol 4 (D10 uplink TX, D0 / D1 branch RX, D7 command RX). That firmware is not written yet; scanner firmware 0.8.0 does not run on this deck. See [README: Firmware and pins](README.md#firmware-and-pins-both-builds).

## Decisions before building

Make these choices before ordering: each one changes which boards, parts and steps you need.

| # | Decision | Option | Label | What it changes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Which duck spacing? | The H50327 duck <!--p:DECK_VARIANTS-->15 mm<!--/p--> in front of each face (recommended, `docs/ANTENNA_SELECTION.md`) | `[D15]` | Order `deck_d15`, <!--p:DECK_DIAMETER_D15-->144 mm<!--/p--> round. A second d15 deck turned over can stand in for the end plate. |
|  |  | <!--p:DECK_VARIANTS-->31 mm<!--/p--> | `[D31]` | Order `deck_d31`, <!--p:DECK_DIAMETER_D31-->146.3 mm<!--/p--> round. Use the end plate PCB, not a second deck. |
| 2 | Which board is the top? | Deck on top, end plate at the bottom; the mast hangs from its pipe | `[Hanging]` | The layout the boards are drawn for: the pipe comes down through the deck's <!--p:ADAPTER_HOLE-->22.2 mm<!--/p--> hole to the end plate, where the adapter's shoulder sits inside the core and a lock nut clamps it from below. The ducks hang below the deck. |
|  |  | Deck at the bottom, on a post or base; end plate on top | `[Upright]` | Not what the boards are drawn for and not modelled: the ducks point up and the adapter / lock nut seat moves to the deck. Check the clamp and the RF before choosing it. |
| 3 | Will you use 1/2 in PVC pipe? | Yes: 1/2 in Sch 40 PVC (<!--p:PIPE_OD-->21.3 mm<!--/p--> OD) and a 1/2 in male adapter | `[Pipe]` | Break out the deck knockout; the end plate takes the adapter and a 1/2 in IPS faucet lock nut. Ethernet and the J1 harness run inside the pipe. Another pipe size: change `ADAPTER_HOLE` and regenerate. |
|  |  | No: mount on the deck's three M3 collar holes | `[No pipe]` | Both knockouts stay in (the end plate can carry a downward antenna in its <!--p:HOLE_RPSMA-->6.5 mm<!--/p--> hole). A collar or bracket on the <!--p:COLLAR_HOLE-->3.4 mm<!--/p--> M3 holes at r <!--p:M3_POS-->25.75 mm<!--/p-->; another route for the cables. |
| 4 | How will you mount it, and to what? | Your answer: ceiling junction box, wall bracket, post, or a housing | - | With `[Pipe]`: sets the pipe length, the adapter thread and the bracket; with `[No pipe]`: the collar or bracket. Also decides whether the mast lifts out of its housing on one nut. Nothing for this is designed in the repo yet: write down what you choose. |
| 5 | Will you fit the end plate? | Yes: the end plate PCB, or with 15 mm ducks a second deck turned over | `[End plate]` | Gussets, M4 bolts and nuts for a second plate; the pipe's lock nut seats on it. |
| 6 | Where are the ESP32 and the power source? | ESP32-S3-ETH with PoE on board, on the pipe above the deck | `[PoE on gateway]` | One Ethernet cable to the mast. The gateway feeds the deck 5 V through J1 pin 1; no J2, no splitter. |
|  |  | ESP32-S3-ETH and a separate PoE splitter (5 V out), both on the pipe | `[PoE splitter]` | J2 fitted; the splitter lead goes into J2 and the deck feeds the gateway through J1 pin 1. Room for the splitter on the pipe. |
|  |  | ESP32-S3-ETH on Ethernet without PoE, 5 V from a USB supply | `[USB power]` | Two cables to the mast (Ethernet and USB). J2 fitted with a USB-C pigtail lead. |

## Boards to order

Gerbers are in [`out/`](out/). Order the deck that matches your duck spacing. Every fab takes at least <!--p:FAB_MIN_QTY-->5<!--/p--> of a design, so the order columns round up to that.

| Board | Applies to | File | Size | Per mast | Order, 1 mast | Order, 3 masts |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Deck, <!--p:DECK_VARIANTS-->15 mm<!--/p--> ducks: the shield plate the antennas go through, with the three scanners on top | `[D15]` | `out/deck_d15_gerbers.zip` | <!--p:DECK_DIAMETER_D15-->144 mm<!--/p--> round | 1 | 5 | 5 |
| Deck, <!--p:DECK_VARIANTS-->31 mm<!--/p--> ducks: the same deck with the D holes <!--p:DECK_VARIANTS-->31 mm<!--/p--> off the faces | `[D31]` | `out/deck_d31_gerbers.zip` | <!--p:DECK_DIAMETER_D31-->146.3 mm<!--/p--> round | 1 | 5 | 5 |
| Face: one side of the triangle reflector core | `[All builds]` | `out/face_pcb_gerbers.zip` | <!--p:FACE_SIZE-->120 x 123.2 mm<!--/p--> with the tabs | 3 | 5 | 10 |
| Corner gusset: holds an M4 nut in a core corner so a plate bolts on | `[All builds]` | `out/gusset_pcb_gerbers.zip` | <!--p:GUSSET_SIZE-->21.3 x 13.3 mm<!--/p--> | 3 (6 with `[End plate]`) | 10 | 20 |
| End plate: a second shield plate across the far end of the triangle | `[End plate]` | `out/endplate_pcb_gerbers.zip` | <!--p:ENDPLATE_DIAMETER-->144 mm<!--/p--> round | 1 | 5 | 5 |

`[D15]` With <!--p:DECK_VARIANTS-->15 mm<!--/p--> ducks a second deck board turned over (bottom to the core) can replace the end plate; the RF model gives the same result. At <!--p:DECK_VARIANTS-->31 mm<!--/p--> the deck is too big for that: use the end plate PCB.

**Fab settings, all boards:** 2 layers, FR-4 (TG130 or better), <!--p:FACE_THICK-->1.6 mm<!--/p-->, 1 oz outer copper, HASL lead-free or ENIG (the exposed copper must take solder), white silkscreen on **both sides**, any solder mask colour, finished hole sizes, single pieces, quantity <!--p:FAB_MIN_QTY-->5<!--/p-->. Smallest holes: <!--p:VIA-->0.4 mm<!--/p--> vias, <!--p:FAB_NPTH_MIN-->0.5 mm<!--/p--> mouse bites.

**Fabs:** JLCPCB or PCBWay (or any fab: the Gerbers are standard RS-274X). The boards are generated and DRC-checked against the fab rules in [`fab/board_rules.csv`](../../fab/board_rules.csv), the stricter of the two; see [README: Fab rules](README.md#fab-rules). Check each board in the fab's Gerber viewer before paying.

**Notes to the fab:**

- Deck: "Round board, <!--p:SLOT_COUNT-->9<!--/p--> milled slots <!--p:SLOT_W-->2 mm<!--/p--> wide (non-plated) and a routed centre knockout ring with mouse-bite bridges (keep the bridges). Large copper pour on the bottom is intentional (RF shield)."
- Face: "Tabs on two edges. Solid copper both sides is intentional (RF reflector)."
- `[End plate]` End plate: "Round board, <!--p:SLOT_COUNT-->9<!--/p--> milled slots <!--p:SLOT_W-->2 mm<!--/p--> wide and a routed knockout ring with mouse-bite bridges (keep the bridges). Solid copper both sides is intentional (RF shield)."

## Before ordering: check a 1:1 print

[`out/pcb_print_1to1.pdf`](out/pcb_print_1to1.pdf) has the boards at 1:1 (both decks top and bottom, a face, the end plate inside and outside, a gusset) and the design formulas page with the radio placement. Print at 100% ("Actual size", not "Fit to page"), then lay the real parts on it.

- [ ] Measure both 100 mm scale bars on every page.
- [ ] XIAOs on their pads, castellations on the pads, IPEX4 on its circle: the outer pad corners have no spare against the <!--p:CORE_MARGIN-->1 mm<!--/p--> core margin.
- [ ] A USB-C plug in each drawn plug path.
- [ ] J1 outline (fitted on the bottom).
- [ ] `[PoE splitter]` `[USB power]` J2 outline (fitted on the bottom).
- [ ] Tie mounts on their <!--p:MOUNT_SQ-->12.5 mm<!--/p--> squares, each pigtail run to its sector's hole.
- [ ] RP-SMAs in the D holes; M3 washers on the <!--p:M3_KEEPOUT-->10 mm<!--/p--> circles; M4 washers on their pads.
- [ ] `[Pipe]` Pipe adapter in the <!--p:ADAPTER_HOLE-->22.2 mm<!--/p--> hole; nothing tall inside <!--p:DECK_CENTRE_CLEAR-->39 mm<!--/p--> across the centre.
- [ ] Face tabs against the deck slots; a gusset against its face slots.
- [ ] `[End plate]` `[Pipe]` End plate: adapter and lock nut in the knockout ring.
- [ ] `[End plate]` `[Pipe]` A pigtail through a knockout ring gap: the IPEX4 plug edge-on in a <!--p:KO_CHANNEL-->2 mm<!--/p--> x <!--p:KO_GAP_L-->10.9 mm<!--/p--> gap (`KO_CHANNEL`; widen it if tight).
- [ ] C1 bulk capacitor: choose an 8 mm radial can at r 19.5 mm, 194 deg (about 33 mm from J2), a 6.3 mm can at r 19 mm, 300 deg (about 7 mm from J2), or none. If fitted: 330 uF, 10 V or more, low ESR.

## Assembly

Solder the faces before any parts go on: the XIAO pads sit close to the seam strip, so seam heat on a populated board can lift them. The deck's silkscreen carries the same list. To rework a seam later, remove the XIAOs first (`out/deck_d15_part_clearance.csv`).

1. `[Pipe]` **Deck knockout:** break out the centre knockout and file the bridge nubs flush so the pipe adapter passes. A deck used as the end plate keeps its knockout unless the pipe goes through it.
1. `[No pipe]` **Deck knockout:** leave it in.
1. **Faces:** drop all three faces' tabs into the deck slots, and the end plate slots if fitted, together as a dry fit; tack the faces to each other, check, then solder the face-to-face seams. With both plates fitted no squareness jig is needed.
1. **Gussets:** push a gusset into each corner's slot pair at each bolted plate, M4 nut on the side away from the plate (a bolt through the plate hole lines it up), then solder the tabs inside and out, and the nut.
1. **Plates:** bolt the deck, and the end plate if fitted, on with M4 x 14 cap bolts and washers, snug (0.5-1 N.m). For a permanent build, solder or tape the plate seams too.
1. **Clean** with IPA.
1. **J1** on the bottom of the deck, housing inside the core, deep side toward the rim; cut the pins flush on top. Seen from the top, pin 1 (square pad) is at the counter-clockwise end.
1. `[PoE splitter]` `[USB power]` **J2** the same way.
1. **XIAOs** U2-U4, castellations on the lengthened pads, USB-C end out toward the corner.
1. **Antennas:** RP-SMA pigtails into the D holes, IPEX4 onto each XIAO, tie mounts on their squares, each pigtail tied inline (it leaves the IPEX4 at <!--p:PIGTAIL_ANGLE-->248 deg<!--/p--> in the corner frame, toward its own sector).
1. `[PoE splitter]` **Power:** the splitter lead into J2.
1. `[USB power]` **Power:** the USB-C pigtail lead into J2.
1. `[PoE on gateway]` **Power:** nothing on J2; the gateway feeds 5 V through the J1 harness.
1. **Gateway:** the J1 harness to the ESP32 (wiring in [README: Deck](README.md#deck)).

## Mounting

- `[Pipe]` The pipe comes down through the deck's <!--p:ADAPTER_HOLE-->22.2 mm<!--/p--> hole. With the end plate, the 1/2 in male adapter's shoulder sits on the plate inside the core, its thread goes down through the broken-out knockout, and the lock nut clamps it from below (mechanical only).
- `[No pipe]` Three <!--p:COLLAR_HOLE-->3.4 mm<!--/p--> M3 holes at r <!--p:M3_POS-->25.75 mm<!--/p--> register the deck to a collar or bracket; keep tracks out of their <!--p:M3_KEEPOUT-->10 mm<!--/p--> washer circles.
- Each plate comes off with its three M4 bolts: the way to the XIAOs' USB-C ports.
- The whole assembly should come out of its housing by removing one nut on the post. Check this on the dry fit.
